newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany will find '97 budget cash for Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Germany will find '97 budget cash for Eurofighter.

text.p: Germany will release funds to help finance production of the Eurofighter combat aircraft despite planned cuts in the 1997 defence budget, a government budget spokesman said on Friday.

Dietrich Austermann of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats repudiated opposition criticism that there would not be enough cash in state coffers to make Germany's contribution to the four-country fighter project.
Austerman told parliament: "Everybody agrees that a new fighter aircraft is needed. It will create 18,000-20,000 new jobs in Germany."

Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and newspaper commentators this week questioned whether planned government spending cuts of 50 billion marks next year would leave room for Eurofighter -- which is running late and over budget.

Germany plans to take delivery of 140 Eurofighters between 2002 and 2012 to replace its existing combat force of Phantom F-4F and MiG-29 jets. A further 40 Eurofighters are intended to replace Tornado jets after 2012.
The defence ministry had no immediate comment, but this week it dismissed the concerns and said the money would be found both this year and next.
The government will only decide later this year, when parliament is due to approve the purchase, when to place its order with the Eurofighter consortium.
Kohl set defence spending at 46.6 billion marks ($30.79 billion) next year, down from 47.1 billion this year and below the 48.5 billion Defence Minister Volker Ruehe had originally been promised.
Bonn is still negotiating on price with consortium partners British Aerospace, Daimler Aerospace, Alenia SpA of Italy and Spain's CASA.
